subject: physics
title: Circular motion
key_idea: An object moving in a circle at constant speed has a changing velocity, because its direction keeps changing. So it is accelerating. This needs a resultant force towards the centre, called the centripetal force.

blocks.text: An object moving in a circle at constant speed does not have constant velocity. This section explains why.

items.meaning: How fast an object moves. It has size only, so it is a scalar.
Speed in a given direction. It has size and direction, so it is a vector.
A change in velocity. It happens when the speed or the direction changes.

items: On a circle, the direction of motion is always changing.
So the velocity is always changing, even though the speed is constant.
A change in velocity is an acceleration, so the object is accelerating.

diagram.alt: Pick a moving object to see what changes and what does not.
diagram.prompt: Pick an object moving at a steady speed

options.label: Satellite in a circular orbit
results: Not zero: gravity, towards the centre of the orbit

options.label: Rubber bung whirled on a string
results: Not zero: the pull of the string, towards the centre

options.label: Car going round a roundabout
results: Not zero: towards the centre of the roundabout

options.label: Car on a straight road
results: Constant: same speed and same direction

options.label: Car speeding up on a straight road
results: Not zero: in the direction of travel

items: Speed can stay constant while velocity changes.
Velocity is a vector, so a change of direction is a change of velocity.
An object moving in a circle at constant speed is accelerating.

blocks.text: An accelerating object must have a resultant force on it. For circular motion this force is called the centripetal force.

diagram.alt: The chain of reasoning from changing direction to a force towards the centre.
steps: The direction of motion keeps changing
So there is a resultant force
The force acts towards the centre of the circle

items.meaning: The resultant force on an object moving in a circle. It acts towards the centre of the circle.

items: A rubber bung whirled on a string: the pull of the string acts towards your hand.
A car round a bend or roundabout: the resultant force acts towards the centre.
If the force stops, the object moves off in a straight line.
Gravity provides the force that keeps planets, moons and satellites in circular orbits.
The force of gravity changes the velocity of the orbiting object but not its speed.
A resultant force towards the centre of the circle is needed to keep an object moving in a circle.
This force is called the centripetal force.
For an orbit, gravity provides the centripetal force.

checks.q: A car goes round a roundabout at a constant 8 m/s. Explain why its velocity is changing.
checks.a: Velocity is a vector with direction. The direction of the car keeps changing, so the velocity changes.

checks.q: What is the name and direction of the resultant force on an object moving in a circle?
checks.a: The centripetal force. It acts towards the centre of the circle.

checks.q: A student says: constant speed means zero acceleration. Is this correct for a satellite in orbit?
checks.a: No. The direction keeps changing, so the velocity changes. The satellite is accelerating towards the centre of the orbit.

exam_phrases: a gravitational / centripetal / resultant force acts on the satellite
the satellite accelerates (towards the centre of the orbit)
the direction changes (which changes the velocity)
(force of) gravity causes the satellite to accelerate (towards the Earth)

mistakes.wrong: The acceleration of the satellite causes its speed to change.
mistakes.right: Acceleration does not change the speed here. It changes the direction, and that changes the velocity.

mistakes.wrong: The velocity is constant because the speed is constant.
mistakes.right: Velocity includes direction. The direction changes, so the velocity changes.

worked_example.question:
The James Webb Space Telescope is an artificial satellite that orbits the Sun at a constant speed.

Explain why the velocity of the satellite changes as it orbits the Sun.
answer_points: A gravitational (centripetal, resultant) force acts on the satellite
So the satellite accelerates towards the centre of the orbit
So the direction changes, which changes the velocity
worked_example.tip: Do not accept 'acceleration causes a change in speed'. The speed stays constant.

blocks.text: (Higher tier) Changing velocity with unchanged speed in an orbit is examined on the Higher tier. This is Physics only.
(Higher tier) For a stable orbit, the radius must change if the speed changes.

exam_phrases: there is a resultant force (on the satellite)
velocity is speed in a (certain) direction

mistakes.wrong: The satellite is not accelerating because its speed is constant.
mistakes.right: The velocity is changing because the direction is changing, so the satellite is accelerating.

mistakes.wrong: The velocity is constant because the speed is constant.
mistakes.right: Velocity is a vector. A change of direction means the velocity is not constant.

worked_example.question:
An artificial satellite is in orbit around the Earth.
The satellite travels at a constant speed around the Earth.

Explain why the satellite is accelerating even though it travels at a constant speed.
answer_points: There is a resultant force on the satellite
worked_example.tip: Any two points score. The direction of the velocity is changing scores both marks.

exam_phrases: acceleration / velocity has magnitude and direction
Velocity is speed in a given / known direction

mistakes.wrong: The velocity of the telescope increases or decreases as it moves round.
mistakes.right: The speed stays constant. The velocity changes only because the direction changes.

mistakes.wrong: The telescope has constant speed, so it has constant velocity.
mistakes.right: Velocity has magnitude and direction. The direction constantly changes, so the velocity changes.

worked_example.question:
The James Webb space telescope orbits the Sun in a circular orbit.

The telescope is accelerating towards the Sun.
Explain why the telescope is accelerating even though its speed remains constant.
worked_example.tip: Ignore answers saying the velocity increases or decreases.
